To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

VIP inhibits the cholinergic and NANC neural bronchoconstriction in the guinea-pig trachea and bronchi, and the exogenously applied acetylcholine and sensory neuropeptides in the trachea and the bronchi.
VIP inhibits cholinergic and NANC bronchoconstictor responses to EFS and the exogenous application of ACh and SP in guinea pig trachea and bronchi.
VIP is a functional antagonist of neural bronchoconstrector responses to ENS and SNS activation in guinea pig trachea and bronchi.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP) on neural bronchoconstriction in guinea pig isolated tracheal and bronchial preparations.
the role of vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP) in airway function.
the role of VIP in the modulation of cholinergic and NANC broncho-constrictor responses to neural stimulation in guinea pig respiratory tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VIP inhibits cholinergic and NANC bronchocontractions by acting at both pre- and post-junctional sites in guinea pig bronchi, but only at the post-junctional level in guinea pig trachea.
VIP is a modulator of neural bronchoactive responses to EFS.
VIP is a potent modulator of neural bronchoconstrector responses in the trachea and bronchi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

VIP is an important modulator of neural broncho-constrictor responses in guinea pig trachea and main bronchi, and that it may have therapeutic potential for the treatment of asthma and chronic bronchitis.
VIP inhibits cholinergic and NANC bronchocontrictor neural responses in guinea pig trachea and bronchi by a prejunctional action and by a postjunctional action on the contractile apparatus.

VIP has a dual action on neural bronchoconstriction, acting both pre- and post-junctionally to modulate release of neurotransmitter and also to modulate post-junctional responses to exogenus transmitters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VIP has a potent inhibitory effect on bronchial smooth muscle contractility.
VIP can modulate neural bronchoconstriction in airways and may therefore have a role in the modulation of bronchoconstrictive responses to a variety of stimuli.
VIP may be involved in regulating the cholinergic and sensory nerve-mediated responses in the guine pig respiratory tract.
